analysis.answer: Under current law, counties decide for themselves whether to honor federal immigration detainers. This measure prohibits all county jails from holding individuals beyond their normal release time solely on the basis of such a detainer.

Local jails will release individuals once their state or local matters are resolved, regardless of federal detainer requests. Federal immigration authorities will have to either take custody of individuals prior to their local release or apprehend them in the community.

The measure addresses the issue of individuals being held in local custody without active local or state charges. The mechanism directly reaches this by banning county jails from honoring federal administrative requests to extend detention.

The state government gains authority over immigration-detention policy at the expense of county governments. Detained individuals gain the certainty of release once local charges are cleared. Federal immigration authorities lose the ability to rely on local jails to hold individuals on their behalf.
